review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its lemmas are used. The related definitions are in Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/BoundedLinearMaps.lean, where `IsBoundedBilinearMap.deriv_apply` is already `@[simp]`. The `fun_prop` attributes cover the HasFDerivAt, HasFDerivWithinAt, HasStrictFDerivAt and Differentiable lemmas. The equational lemmas `IsBoundedBilinearMap.fderiv`, `IsBoundedBilinearMap.fderivWithin`, `ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv_of_bilinear` and `ContinuousLinearMap.fderivWithin_of_bilinear` are not simp. That looks deliberate. The `of_bilinear` versions need differentiability hypotheses, and their right-hand sides expand into `precompR` and `precompL` sums. The `IsBoundedBilinearMap` ones take an explicit hypothesis `h` that simp would have to synthesise. I found only two uses of the `of_bilinear` lemmas, both explicit calls (Calculus/VectorField.lean:574 and Calculus/ContDiff/Bounds.lean:102). Nothing shows that simp would help there. I found no competing rules, no rewrites in the wrong direction and no plausible cycles. I could not run Lean, so I made no simplifier-behaviour claims.
